diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepeat actions that fail to change state, especially clicks, no-ops, and scrolling, instead of switching approach or terminating.
expected_mechanism: State-change checks interrupt unproductive loops and force a different tactic after repeated non-progress. This should reduce redundant operations and repeated interaction errors; the cost is extra state comparison and occasional premature strategy changes when progress is delayed.
policy_text: After any action, verify an observable state change relevant to the goal. If the same or equivalent action produces no relevant change twice, do not repeat it: reassess assumptions, inspect current state, and choose a materially different action. If no viable alternative exists, stop and report the blocker.

quantitative_evidence.finding: result:repeated has +1,261 operations (candidate/bad excess), 11.31% of the profile's 11,146 absolute differential operations. Within this excess, click contributes +639, noop +356, and scroll +277; fill (-12) and select_option (-21) favor base/good.

Inspection/navigation/wait paths contain +1,264 repeated outcomes and +1,562 progress outcomes; repeated behavior is therefore broadly associated with these recurring interaction strategies, not one task-specific object.

After excluding progress and repetition, the largest remaining candidate excesses are failed clicks: +148 invisible-element errors and +129 click timeouts, consistent with persisting in ineffective interactions. Base/good instead has 92 more terminal outcomes and 67 more conclusions.
